assumptions: Planting is possible on the first day the trailing 10-day rainfall sum reaches the threshold, having been below it before, with root-zone soil wetness at or above 0.40. This is an assumption, not a sourced rule.
This figure is the day the 10-day threshold is first met, not the first rain day. It can lag the first rain by up to 9 days.

rule_rows.source: National Research Council (1996), Lost Crops of Africa Vol. I, chapter 2
rule_rows.page_or_quote: Page 57, section High Temperature: "Finger millet thrives under hot conditions. It can grow where temperatures are as high as 35°C. In Uganda, the crop grows best where the average maximum temperature exceeds 27°C and the average minimum does not fall below 18°C."
rule_rows.note: cross-check row, not a range. The chapter gives a growth ceiling of 35 C and a Uganda average-minimum floor of 18 C, which is not an optimum pair, so it is left out of value_min and value_max. The EcoCrop row beside it supplies the range the app reads

crop_limitations: Finger millet planting dates for Soroti are borrowed from the MAAIF maize window. No Soroti millet calendar was found
